## Positioning

Two skill sets that rarely appear in the same person:

1. **Domain depth in billing and reconciliation.** A 26-year career on telecom billing systems, where
   correctness is the product — an error is an incorrect charge or an incorrect tax filing, not
   a cosmetic defect.
2. **Current delivery capability.** Two products shipped to production over the past year,
   built by directing AI coding agents, with unit tests, end-to-end Playwright specs and deploy
   pipelines that include a rehearsed rollback.

## Career

### Objective Solutions — March 1999 to December 2023

26 years: 15 as Senior Developer (Smalltalk, Java, PL/SQL on Oracle), around 10 as Consultant, and the most recent as Senior Data Analyst at Eleflow.

- **Telecom billing**: development and maintenance of the Diginet product and its successor,
  Objective NG.
- **Data warehouses**: built the Billing and Tax data warehouses in PL/SQL.
- **Reconciliation consulting**: tax, accounting and financial reconciliation, including
  credit-card reconciliation for Adiq, a card acquirer.
- **Functional analysis in Scrum**: at Adiq (Feb 2019 – Mar 2020), owned the functional
  specification of the reconciliation system — user stories and acceptance criteria per feature,
  every sprint, with the solution designed together with the architect.
- **Consulting presentations**: at Netserv, On and HughesNet, on billing, collections, tax,
  accounting and reconciliation.
- **Healthcare**: focal point for medical claims at PreventSenior.
- **Data migrations**: four end-to-end migrations — Oi Cabo (100,000 subscribers), Compuserve
  (35,000), On (10,000), Netserv (10,000).
- **Sky**: when Sky moved off Diginet, the client's own migration team asked for him to produce
  the reports covering their 1 million subscriber base.
- **Named clients**: Sky, Telefônica/Vivo, HughesNet, Netserv, PreventSenior.

### Eleflow — 2024 to 2025

Senior Data Analyst. Oracle to BigQuery data migration, in a Scrum team.

## Products in production

### Portal Brasileirão

**URL**: https://brasileirao.mpbarbosa.com
**Repo**: https://github.com/mpbarbosa/portal_brasileirao
Companion app for the Brazilian Série A championship.

- Stack: React 19, TypeScript, Express 5, Tailwind 4, AWS
- 1,523 unit tests, 46 end-to-end Playwright specs
- 905 commits in five weeks (23 August–30 September 2026)
- 7 GitHub Actions workflows including rollback, with a documented flip-back drill
- Keyless deploys over OIDC; OAuth login; Material Design 3 tokens
- Live `/api/health` endpoint
- Falls back to a frozen snapshot when no API token is available

### Agora na Copa 2026

**URL**: https://copa2026.mpbarbosa.com
**Repo**: https://github.com/mpbarbosa/agora_na_copa_2026
Companion app for the FIFA World Cup 2026.

- Stack: React 19, TypeScript, Express, AWS
- 283 unit tests, 37 end-to-end Playwright specs
- 1,204 commits
- Monte Carlo qualification simulator using a Dixon-Coles model, applying the Article 13 FIFA
  tie-breaking criteria in the correct order
- External integrations with per-integration fallbacks: FIFA API, Open-Meteo, Google Trends
- Served by nginx and systemd

## Projects and tooling

### ai_workflow

**Repo**: https://github.com/mpbarbosa/ai_workflow
**License**: MIT
**Languages**: Bash (orchestration), Node.js (tooling), Python (utilities)

Automation pipeline that makes AI-assisted development verifiable — validating code quality,
documentation and test coverage so teams can trust what any AI coding tool generates before it
ships. Supports GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude and other AI coding tools.

The mission is separately seeking public investment on Singularity; that content lives at
https://mpbarbosa.com/en/singularity/ and is deliberately kept off the hiring pages.

### conversando_com_pessoa

**Repo**: https://github.com/mpbarbosa/conversando_com_pessoa
**Languages**: Python
**Status**: Public since October 2026. Runs locally; not deployed.

Local RAG system. Dense retrieval (multilingual-e5-base) combined with BM25, over an index whose
integrity manifest refuses to load an inconsistent index, plus a plagiarism guard calibrated on
real answers, pluggable generation and a FastAPI web layer. Orchestration is decided by rules,
never by the model.

Retrieval quality, on the gold set published in the repo README — 40 questions, 176 candidates
graded by TREC pooling of both retrievers' top 5: dense nDCG@5 0.719 and apt@3 95%, against BM25
0.488 and 65%. A second, deeper gold set in docs/CONTROLO.md (433 judgments, closed to the top 20)
reports dense 0.606, and 0.696 with reranking. These are two different measurements, not two
versions of the same one, so the gold set has to be named alongside any of these numbers.

292 tests passing, 1 skipped.

### trilhas_estudos

**Repo**: https://github.com/mpbarbosa/trilhas_estudos
**Languages**: Python
**Status**: Public. Runs locally; not deployed.

Study-track control and suggestion system. The domain is modelled in frozen dataclasses with
`mypy --strict` over all of `src/`, and the suggestion engine is rules — there is no model in this
repo.

Two design decisions carry the project. The progress log is event-sourced with UPDATE and DELETE
forbidden by SQLite trigger, so correcting a fact means appending another event and the audit
trail does not depend on the writer's discipline. And the suggestion engine is explainable by
construction: no suggestion exists without the factors that produced it, and the explanation never
cites a factor that is absent from them.

294 tests over 6,772 lines of Python, 16 ADRs, and five CI gates on every push and pull request —
compiled-catalogue check, pytest, ruff check, ruff format and mypy — each across a 3.12/3.14
matrix.
